## ip_locations: Where the IP addresses in the records are registered
IP address 198.51.100.40 — according to Example IP Database, 2025-10-01: registered to Example Broadband (AS64503), location Example City, Example Region, Exampleland (accuracy about 20 km). (E4)
An IP location is the provider's estimate of where the network is registered or used. It can differ from where the person was, for example on mobile data, a VPN or a hosting service. Addresses can be reassigned over time; this lookup used a database dated 2025-10-01.
## account_access_sequence: The sequence the records show
- 1. The complainant states that they entered their credentials, card details or a one-time code on a fake website or app.
- 2. The institution's record shows a digital token activated at 20:10 on 12 September 2025 on a device labelled 'Phone model EX-300'. The record shows the activation was authorised by SMS one-time code, sent to registered mobile number. (E4)
- 3. The complainant states that this device is not theirs.
- 4. The record shows an alert about the activation sent at 20:10 on 12 September 2025 to cardholder@example.com. (E4)
- 5. The record shows a login at 20:15 on 12 September 2025 from this device, authorised by digital token. (E4)
- 6. The record shows the card ending 0001 added to a mobile wallet at 20:32 on 12 September 2025 on a device labelled 'Phone model EX-300', authorised by the digital token. (E6)
- 7. The record shows 3 card payments totalling S$7,550 between 20:48 on 12 September 2025 and 00:15 on 13 September 2025, authenticated by 3-D Secure with the digital token. (E6)
- 8. On the records provided, 3 of these payments were authenticated through 3-D Secure using the digital token activated at 20:10 on 12 September 2025. (E4, E6)
- 9. The complainant reported to the institution on 13 September 2025. The record shows the card blocked at 08:45 on 13 September 2025. (E4)
Card scheme rules are an agreement between the card scheme and the card issuer. The cardholder is not a party to them. They are shown here as the process available to the issuer.
This pack holds selected sections of Visa's rules, edition dated 1 March 2025, on how unauthorised payments are handled. It does not hold the full rules. (R1)

The institution's letter states that it did not raise a dispute because 'the payments were authenticated with the registered digital token'. (E2)

## card_dispute_comparison: Card scheme rules on disputing the card payments
Card scheme rules are an agreement between the card scheme and the card issuer. The cardholder is not a party to them. They are shown here as the process available to the issuer.
This pack holds selected sections of Visa's rules (Synthetic scheme rules V), edition dated Synthetic edition, on how unauthorised payments are handled. It does not hold the full rules. (R1)
- payment date: 12 September 2025; amount: SGD 1,980.00; Merchant: Example Electronics Store; card last4: 0001; scheme: Visa; Entry mode: an online (card-absent) payment; Authentication: 3-D Secure approved with a digital token; authentication result: authenticated; Device: Phone model EX-300 (E1, E6)
Record: The complainant disputes the payment of SGD 1,980.00 on 12 September 2025 as not made or authorised by them. The complainant states that the device labelled 'Phone model EX-300' is not theirs. (E1)
Expected: Section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V, version Synthetic edition: "Under Synthetic scheme rules V, section 11.8.5, edition Synthetic edition, Dispute Condition 10.4 applies where the cardholder denies authorising or taking part in the payment." (R1)
Side by side: The complainant disputes the payment of SGD 1,980.00 on 12 September 2025 as not made or authorised by them. The complainant states that the device labelled 'Phone model EX-300' is not theirs. The record shows this, as the document expects.
Record: The record shows the payment was an online (card-absent) payment. (E6)
Expected: Section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V, version Synthetic edition: "Under Synthetic scheme rules V, section 11.8.5, edition Synthetic edition, Dispute Condition 10.4 covers payments in a card-absent environment." (R1)
Side by side: The record shows the payment was an online (card-absent) payment, as the document expects.
Record: The record shows the payment authenticated by 3-D Secure approved with a digital token, result 'authenticated'. The record does not show the electronic commerce indicator or the authentication values sent with the authorisation. (E6)
Expected: Section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V, version Synthetic edition: "Under Synthetic scheme rules V, section 11.8.5, edition Synthetic edition, the invalid disputes for Dispute Condition 10.4 include payments authenticated through Visa Secure, payments where Visa Secure authentication was attempted, and payments with an authenticated token where cardholder verification was approved." (R1)
Side by side: The document expects what section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V (R1) sets out. The record shows the payment authenticated by 3-D Secure approved with a digital token, result 'authenticated'. The record does not show the electronic commerce indicator or the authentication values sent with the authorisation.
Record: The payment is dated 12 September 2025; the complainant asked the institution to dispute it on 14 September 2025, 2 calendar days later. The records do not show the date the payment was processed by the scheme; the count runs from the payment date. (E1, E5)
Expected: Section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V, version Synthetic edition: "Under Synthetic scheme rules V, section 11.8.5, edition Synthetic edition, the time limit for Dispute Condition 10.4 is 120 calendar days from the date the payment was processed." (R1)
Side by side: The payment is dated 12 September 2025; the complainant asked the institution to dispute it on 14 September 2025, 2 calendar days later. The records do not show the date the payment was processed by the scheme; the count runs from the payment date. The record shows this, as the document expects.

Expected: Section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V, version Synthetic edition: "Under Synthetic scheme rules V, section 11.8.5, edition Synthetic edition, the issuer is to report the payment to Visa as fraud before raising the dispute." (R1)
Side by side: The records provided do not show whether what section 11.8.5 of the Synthetic scheme rules V (R1) sets out took place.

## customer_conduct_comparison: The conduct the records show, and what each document refers to
The complainant states that they entered their credentials, card details or a one-time code on a fake website or app.
The ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards does not refer to entering credentials, card details or a code on a website or app.
The record shows 3 card payments authenticated by 3-D Secure with the digital token on the device labelled 'Phone model EX-300'. The complainant states that the device labelled 'Phone model EX-300' is not theirs. (E6)
The records do not show who approved these payments. (E6)
The record shows 1 alert, the first sent at 20:10 on 12 September 2025 to cardholder@example.com. The complainant reported to the institution on 13 September 2025, 1 calendar day after the first alert. (E4)
The ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards does not refer to notifications and alerts from the institution.
The record shows access blocked at 08:45 on 13 September 2025, channel recorded as 'hotline'. (E4)
The ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards does not refer to blocking access.
The records provided do not show whether or when a police report was made.
The ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards does not refer to reporting to the police.
The institution's letter describes the complainant's conduct as 'grossly negligent'. The conduct it cites is entered card details and a one-time code on a website reached from a message. (E2)
The ABS Code of Practice for Banks – Credit Cards uses the term 'gross negligence'. (R4)
The institution's own terms in force on 12 September 2025 are not held for that date.
